verdict.rationale: Yapily's evidence covers a developer API/SDKs and an MCP-served documentation assistant for coding agents (yapily-docs-6, yapily-probe-3), but there is no evidence that end users can issue natural-language commands to actually operate Yapily's core functions (payments, account data retrieval, etc.). The MCP/llms.txt integration is for helping coding agents navigate docs, not a natural-language control interface for the product's operations.
